chapterNote: The thanksgiving that answers Psalm 20. There the people prayed for their king before battle — may He give you what your heart desires — and here they thank God afterward in the same words: You have given him what his heart desired and have not withheld the request of his lips. Everything the king has is listed as a gift: blessings that arrived before he asked, a crown of pure gold set on his head by God's hands, life when he asked for life — length of days forever and ever, more than any mortal king could use — glory, splendor and majesty laid on him, and the joy of God's face. The one thing the king contributes to his own security is trust, and through the covenant love of the Most High he will not be shaken. Then the other side: the same hand that crowned him will find every enemy; the same face that gladdened him will turn them into a blazing oven; their schemes will fail and their line will end. The last line hands the whole thing back where it belongs: be exalted, O LORD, in Your strength — we will sing to Your might, not the king's. Christian readers have always heard, under 'length of days forever and ever,' the one Son of David of whom it is simply true.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. O LORD, the king rejoices in Your strength; how greatly he exults in Your salvation!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. The king [melek] shall joy [samach] in Your strength [oz], O LORD [YHWH]; and in Your salvation [yeshuah] how greatly [meod] shall he rejoice [gil — exult]!
1.notes: YHWH be-ozzekha yismach-melekh (H3068, H5797, H8055, H4428): in Your strength the king rejoices — the companion to Psalm 20, where the people prayed for the king before battle; here they thank God for him after it — u-bi-shuatekha mah-yagel meod (H3444, H1523, H3966): in Your salvation how GREATLY he exults. The king's joy is in God's strength, not his own; that is the whole psalm's theology of kingship.

2.text: You have given him what his heart desired and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah.
2.amp: You have given [natan] him his heart's [leb] desire [taavah], and have not withholden [mana] the request [aresheth] of his lips [saphah]. Selah [Selah].
2.notes: taavat libbo natattah lo (H8378, H3820, H5414): his heart's desire GIVEN — va-areshet sephatav bal-manata (H782, H8193, H4513): and the request of his lips not withheld — Psalm 20:4's prayer, 'may He give you what your heart desires', answered in the same words. aresheth, the request, occurs only here in the Bible. Selah: pause on an answered prayer.

3.text: For You come to meet him with rich blessings; You set a crown of pure gold on his head.
3.amp: For You prevent [qadam — come to meet, go before] him with the blessings [berakah] of goodness [tov]: You set [shith] a crown [atarah] of pure gold [paz] on his head [rosh].
3.notes: ki-teqaddemennu birkhot tov (H6923, H1293, H2896): You MEET him — qadam, the old sense of 'prevent', to go before — with blessings of good: grace arriving ahead of the king. tashit le-rosho ateret paz (H7896, H7218, H5850, H6337): You set on his head a crown of paz, refined gold — perhaps the Ammonite crown of 2 Samuel 12:30, but the psalm says God's hands set it there.

4.text: He asked life of You, and You gave it: length of days forever and ever.
4.amp: He asked [shaal] life [chay] of You, and You gave [natan] it him, even length [orek] of days [yom] for ever [olam] and ever [ad].
4.notes: chayyim shaal mimmekha natattah lo (H2416, H7592, H5414): he asked life — survival in battle — and You gave it; orekh yamim olam va-ed (H753, H3117, H5769, H5703): length of days FOREVER AND EVER — more than any king can use. The court hyperbole ('O king, live forever') becomes literal in only one Son of David (cf. Hebrews 7:16; Revelation 1:18), which is why the church reads the psalm of Him.

5.text: His glory is great through Your salvation; splendor and majesty You lay upon him.
5.amp: His glory [kabod] is great [gadol] in Your salvation [yeshuah]: honour [hod — splendor] and majesty [hadar] have You laid [shavah — set] upon him.
5.notes: gadol kebodo bi-shuatekha (H1419, H3519, H3444): his glory is great IN Your salvation — borrowed glory, the reflected kind; hod ve-hadar teshavveh alav (H1935, H1926, H7737): splendor and majesty You LAY on him — the pair that is God's own robe in Psalm 104:1, here draped on the king. What the LORD wears, He lends.

6.text: For You make him a blessing forever; You gladden him with joy in Your presence.
6.amp: For You have made ['set him to be blessings', shith berakah, the KJV margin] him most blessed for ever [ad]: You have made him exceeding glad ['make him glad with joy', chadah simchah, the KJV margin] with Your countenance [panim — face].
6.notes: ki-teshitehu berakhot la-ad (H7896, H1293, H5703): You SET him as blessings, the margin's literal — Abraham's promise, 'be a blessing' (Genesis 12:2), placed on the king: not only blessed but a source of blessing forever. techaddehu be-simchah et-panekha (H2302, H8057, H6440): You make him glad with joy in Your face — Psalm 16:11's fullness of joy in the presence. The king's reward is God's face.

7.text: For the king trusts in the LORD, and through the covenant love of the Most High he will not be shaken.
7.amp: For the king [melek] trusts [batach] in the LORD [YHWH], and through the mercy [chesed — covenant love] of the most High [Elyon] he shall not be moved [mot — shaken].
7.notes: ki-ha-melekh boteach ba-YHWH (H4428, H982, H3068): the king TRUSTS in the LORD — the hinge verse, the one human act the psalm names as the ground of the king's stability — u-be-chesed Elyon bal-yimmot (H2617, H5945, H4131): and in the chesed of the Most High he will not totter. Trust on his side, covenant love on God's; stability is the product.

8.text: Your hand will find out every one of Your enemies; Your right hand will find out all who hate You.
8.amp: Your hand [yad] shall find out [matsa] all Your enemies [oyeb]: Your right hand [yamin] shall find out [matsa] those that hate [sane] You.
8.notes: timtsa yadekha le-khol-oyebekha (H4672, H3027, H341): Your hand will FIND all Your enemies — the psalm turns from what God has done for the king to what He will do to the enemies, and the address turns to the king (or to God; the psalm lets the two blur, which is its point): no hiding place from that hand. yeminekha timtsa soneekha (H3225, H4672, H8130): Your right hand will find those who hate You. Verses 8-12 are the other side of verses 1-7: what the King's strength does to the King's enemies.

9.text: You will make them like a blazing oven in the time of Your presence; the LORD will swallow them up in His wrath, and fire will devour them.
9.amp: You shall make [shith] them as a fiery [esh] oven in the time [et] of Your anger [panim — face, presence]: the LORD [YHWH] shall swallow them up [bala] in His wrath [aph], and the fire [esh] shall devour [akal] them.
9.notes: teshitemo ke-tannur esh le-et panekha (H7896, H784, H6256, H6440): You will set them like an oven of fire at the time of Your FACE — the same panim that gladdened the king in verse 6 consumes his enemies here. YHWH be-appo yeballeem ve-tokhlem esh (H3068, H639, H1104, H398, H784): the LORD in His anger swallows them, fire eats them — Korah's fate (Numbers 16:32-35) as the pattern. One face, two effects.

10.text: Their fruit You will wipe from the earth, their seed from among the sons of men.
10.amp: Their fruit [peri] shall You destroy [abad] from the earth [eretz], and their seed [zera] from among the children [ben] of men [adam].
10.notes: piryamo me-eretz teabbed (H6529, H776, H6): their FRUIT destroyed from the earth — ve-zaram mi-bene adam (H2233, H1121, H120): their seed from among the sons of men. The lasting life God gave the king (v. 4) — in a royal house, a line that does not end — is what the enemies lose: no line, no future. The psalm measures judgment in generations because it measured blessing that way.

11.text: For they intended evil against You and devised a scheme they cannot carry out.
11.amp: For they intended [natah — stretched out] evil [ra] against You: they imagined [chashab — devised] a mischievous device [mezimmah — scheme], which they are not able [yakol] to perform.
11.notes: ki-natu alekha raah (H5186, H7451): they STRETCHED OUT evil against You — natah, the verb of a hand or a cord extended toward its mark: evil reached out and aimed at Him; chashebu mezimmah bal-yukhalu (H2803, H4209, H3201): devised a scheme they cannot pull off — Psalm 2:1's vain plot in one line. The enemies' failure is not for lack of trying.

12.text: For You will make them turn their backs when You aim Your arrows on the string at their faces.
12.amp: Therefore shall You make ['thou shalt set them as a butt', shith, the KJV margin] them turn their back, when You shall make ready [kun] Your arrows upon Your strings against the face [panim] of them.
12.notes: ki teshitemo shekhem (H7896): You will make them 'shoulder' — the margin's literal: turned around, backs to You — or, as the other margin reads, 'set them as a butt', a target; be-metarekha tekhonen al-penehem (H3559, H6440): on Your bowstrings You aim at their faces. The evil they stretched out toward God in verse 11, answered by the bowstring God stretches toward them.

13.text: Be exalted, O LORD, in Your strength! So will we sing and make music to Your might.
13.amp: Be You exalted [rum], LORD [YHWH], in Your own strength [oz]: so will we sing [shir] and praise [zamar — make music to] Your power [geburah — might].
13.notes: rumah YHWH be-uzzekha (H7311, H3068, H5797): be high, LORD, in Your OZ — the strength of verse 1, where the psalm began; nashirah u-nezammerah geburatekha (H7891, H2167, H1369): we will sing and make music to Your might. The king's psalm ends with the people singing not to the king but to the King's God — the only safe place for a nation's pride.
